_: The catalogue's Features cards. Every system of notes/crew/systems-map/systems.json gets a card; these add how a player uses it, the sheet sections with its numbers (vitals SHEET.md headings unless `sheet` names another), and the things it links to (ids, or `match` words found in ids).

body.how: Nine stats on the HUD: health, stamina, food, warmth, breath and more. Eat, rest, stay warm and dry; speed and health change with them.

air.how: The temperature you feel comes from the climate, season, hour, height, rain, wind, water nearby, fires and rooms. Watch the HUD's temperature; dress for it, or stand by a fire.

clothing.how: Wear a hat, coat, trousers and boots of fur, hide, wool or linen (sewn at the crafting table from the cloth and string); armour goes over them. Wet clothes keep less warmth.

rooms.how: Close a room around a fire: its walls and size keep the warmth in.

food.how: Eat a mix: a varied stomach raises max health and stamina. Food keeps fresh, then goes stale and spoils.

meals.how: Put ingredients in the cooking pot over a fire: stews warm and fill from what goes in.

preserve.how: Hang food on the drying rack (still air, a fire below, dry weather) or salt it; it keeps for weeks.

calendar.how: Days run 20 minutes; seasons change day length, the weather and what grows. A new world starts on spring's 8th at 10:00.

weather.how: Rain by season from each biome's climate, wind and fog by biome, lying snow and freezing water. Being wet feels colder and wet clothes keep less warmth.

ley.how: Make a dowsing rod (sticks, string, a tektite) and hold it: it senses the ley lines and their nodes. Waystones sleep on the great crossings, ringed by the ancients' carved stone.

map.how: A map that fills in where you walk, a minimap in the HUD corner, and waystones woken on the ley crossings.

climbing.how: Climb any wall on stamina: slower on smooth stone, never on ice; at the top you mantle over.

glider.how: Craft a leather glider; while falling press jump to open it. It drifts with the day's wind.

grapple.how: Throw the grappling hook (Iron Age: wrought-iron flukes on a cord) up to 22 blocks: it catches on blocks with grip and pulls you over walls.

taming.how: Passive animals are tamed by feeding; wild ones are knocked out (club, tranquilizer darts), kept asleep with a sedative and fed while they sleep. A saddle lets you ride; the spyglass shows an animal's stats, genes and taming from afar.

breeding.how: Tame animals breed by season and bond; egg-layers lay in nests (an egg, then a hatchling). Genes pass on coats, size and personality.

gems.how: Cut a gem at the crafting table from a diamond, peridot, tektite or amber; set it in a part's or built item's socket at the assembly row (cheap gems crack one time in four coming out). Each rolls 1-3 boosts.

drenkaun.how: Make the Wood-Warden's altar and set it among old trees; use it with a forest offering (an acorn, a red mushroom, berries, a moss block). Drenkaun rises: charges, sweeps, stomps and roots; break its antlers and crown for loot. Its heartseed is the Stone Age key's boss part; its calf can be tamed.

skyevents.how: One event a night: blood moons (more monsters), meteor showers and fallen stars, auroras and big impacts. Fallen stars and craters give star steel, pallasite, tektites and eclipse ash.

starmats.how: Mine a fallen meteorite or an impact crater for star steel and pallasite; a starheart in iron makes the star lantern.

firsthours.how: Pick up loose rocks, flint and fallen branches. Sneak and strike a flint nodule on the ground with a rock to open the knapping screen: strike away the squares outside the head's outline. A bow drill or hand drill on a fire bed lights the first fire.

craftbook.how: Make parts at the crafting table (each of a material its shape takes), then put them in the assembly row: head, haft and fitting for tools; blade, grip, guard and pommel for swords; shell, fastening and lining for armour. The parts' materials set the numbers and the look.

waitcrafts.how: Some work takes real days: hides on the tanning frame become leather, in the tanning pit sole leather, logs in the charcoal clamp coal.

crops.how: Find seeds in grass, till with a hoe, sow; crops grow by warmth and water and tire or feed the soil.

soil.how: Grazers leave dung pats; spoiled food becomes compost in the compost bin; fertile soil grows crops faster.

wild.how: Ground cover, ferns, shrubs, young trees, mushrooms and berries by biome: pick them by hand, cut grass for fibre with a flake.

plants.how: Every plant grows by warmth, rain and the soil water where it stands.

trees.how: Fell a tree with an axe: it falls and lies down; branches and bark come off it.

effects.how: Cold, heat, poison, bleeding, sedation, encumbered and well fed show on the HUD and change how you move and heal.

difficulty.how: The base:difficulty world rule scales the body, eating and tames.

levels.how: XP from blocks, crafting, kills, taming and discoveries raises your level; each level gives a perk point.

skills.how: Doing things raises the matching skill (forging raises Smithing, taming raises Taming); a skill's level gates how deep you go in its region of the perk web.

perkweb.how: Open the Skills screen (K): spend perk points on nodes next to ones you have; notables and keystones change how you play, sockets take stones.

sockets.how: Put a found stone in a web socket: Maunduk rolls boosts, Aruduk strengthens the nodes round it, Remaru gives ley sight, Emakaun health by the nodes in its reach.

monsters.how: Hostile mobs come at night and in the dark, more on a blood moon; campfires keep them off.

dimensions.how: A frame of amber blocks lit with a torch opens the gateway to the Cretaceous, a linked world of its own biomes and dinosaurs.

death.how: When you die you drop everything at a grave (a tombstone) and run back for it; a short grace after.

machines.how: Redstone, pistons, observers, dispensers and lamps work today; the Age of Steam's machines come later.

gear.how: A weapon's, tool's or armour's numbers come from the curves by age, through its working part's material.

glow.how: Fireflies by biome and warmth; foxfire and glowing mushrooms light dark forests.
